full_judgment:
4. The plaintiff examined two witnesses namely, PW I MA Akbor, their Administrative Officer and PW 2 Birendra Chandra Shaha their Manager, Finance in support of their claim. The learned Subordinate Judge by the impugned judgment and order decreed the suit and directed to refer the claim of the plaintiff to the Arbitrator for arbitration on the findings, inter alia, that Pakistan Insurance Corporation admitted the loss of the plaintiff due to the riot occurrence at the mills premises of the plaintiff, that the defendant did not deny the claim of the plaintiff by examining any witness, that a riot took place in the mills premises of the plaintiff for which the plaintiff alleged to have incurred a loss to the tune of Tk. 5,83,366.15 and for this it was necessary that the matter regarding the claim of the plaintiff be referred to the Arbitrator for arbitration. Although an issue was framed as to whether the suit was barred by limitation the learned Subordinate Judge recorded no finding on that issue. 

 11. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent, on the other hand, has contended that since the suit was filed within 3 years from the date of the occurrence after excluding the time between 1st of March, 1971 and 1st March, 1972 as provided by President's Order No. of 1972, the suit cannot be said to be barred by limitation. But condition No. 19 of the policies has not prescribed a period of 12 months for filing an application under section 20 of the Arbitration Act. As a matter of fact there is no limitation prescribed for filing such an application under the Limitation Act, 1908. The limitation of 3 years prescribed by Article 181 of the schedule of the Limitation Act is applicable only to application under the Code of Civil Procedure, A reference may be made in this connection to the case of Wazir Chand Mahajan and another Vs. The Union of India, reported in AIR 1967 (SC) 990.
